claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic NbMoTaW.
Untreated equiatomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Untreated NbMoTaW has very poor room-temperature ductility, with a fracture strain below 5%.
Untreated NbMoTaW has excellent mechanical strength at approximately 1600 °C.
First-principles calculations predict irradiation resistance in NbMoTaW.

Solution treatment near 1650 °C followed by annealing near 600 °C and rapid quenching will convert NbMoTaW to an inverted microstructure consisting of a continuous disordered BCC matrix and discrete nanoscale ordered precipitates.
The intermediate anneal promotes ordering, while rapid quenching limits growth and coalescence of the ordered phase.
A continuous ordered B2-like matrix is associated with brittleness and low room-temperature fracture strain.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete ordered precipitates can be produced by solution treatment, annealing at 600 °C, and water quenching.
Percolation of the disordered BCC matrix enhances dislocation mobility and room-temperature plasticity.
Dispersed ordered precipitates will retain the high-temperature load-bearing capability of NbMoTaW at approximately 1600 °C.
The similar BCC structures of the matrix and precipitates will preserve high-temperature mechanical performance.
The similar BCC structures will preserve irradiation resistance by maintaining comparable vacancy and interstitial mobilities and associated defect-recombination mechanisms.
The heat treatment will increase room-temperature fracture strain in NbMoTaW from below 5% to above 30%.
The treated alloy's yield strength at 1600 °C will remain within 10% of the untreated baseline.
After 1-MeV ion irradiation to approximately 8 dpa, the treated alloy will preserve the absence of dislocation-loop clustering.
Excessive phase separation or unwanted brittle secondary phases will negate the proposed benefits.
The intervention is applicable mainly to single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloys with similar or high mixing entropy.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field presents irradiation resistance as an established property of the fabricated alloy, whereas the baseline field qualifies it as a prediction from first-principles calculations rather than an experimentally established property.
